This enzyme is targeted by 2-(3-Ethenyl-4-pyridinyl)ethanol, which in turn has a direct interaction with ZR-75-1. The evidence suggests a chain of targets, where Shinjulactone B acts as a modulator of the pathway by binding to and influencing the activity of Glucose-1-phosphate thymidylyltransferase. This interaction may alter the activity of 2-(3-Ethenyl-4-pyridinyl)ethanol, which then affects ZR-75-1. The integrated explanation highlights the role of Shinjulactone B in modulating the downstream effects of 2-(3-Ethenyl-4-pyridinyl)ethanol, potentially through the regulation of Glucose-1-phosphate thymidylyltransferase. The relationship is supported by a clear, hierarchical pathway that connects the two entities through their shared targets.
